title: The Person Who Needed Help
description: Someone near you is struggling—a person with too many bags, a elderly person crossing the street, a child looking lost, someone crying quietly. You could help. Or you could look away.

outcomes.narration: You approach and offer your help. For a moment they look suspicious—fair enough. But when they accept, genuine relief floods their face. 'Thank you,' they say, 'I really needed this.' You walk away feeling like you've done something that actually matters.

choices.label: Help in a way that preserves their dignity

outcomes.narration: You find a way to help that doesn't draw attention—a quietly opened door, a 'mistaken' extra coffee you hand them, a donation you make in their name without saying a word. The kindest help is the one nobody sees.

You tell yourself someone else will help. Or that they didn't really need it. You keep walking, and the feeling follows you all day—a small weight you can't quite shake. Maybe tomorrow you'll be braver.
